name: TX-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District partisan lean of 24 points toward Republicans
Incumbent Moran has raised $2.3M vs. roughly $20K for Prince
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 2%
No public polling; race rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 24-point Republican lean, Moran's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the Democratic chance near two percent all point the same direction, and no polling or ratings suggest any reason to move away from those fundamentals.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Moran or an extraordinary national wave against Republicans could narrow the margin, and even that would be unlikely to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's first district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 24 points toward the GOP. Nathaniel Moran, first elected in 2022, is seeking another term and has raised about $2.3 million, leaving him with more than $900,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Yolanda Prince has raised roughly $20,000 and reports under $1,500 in cash, leaving her little capacity to compete. No independent polls of the race are available, and prediction markets put the Democratic chance at about two percent.

With no expert ratings and no polling, the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals. A deep-red electorate, an incumbent with a large financial edge, and a minimally funded challenger make a Republican win overwhelmingly likely. The expected margin sits near 20 points Republican, with Democratic prospects close to negligible.
